I've been working this same land for 25 years. I know what this soil wants, and I know what my family needs. With some people in the household working off the farm now, I'm the main one managing these fields. Five mu is not much, but it feeds us and brings in some cash. Let me think through this season.

**Wheat comes first.** I sow in October after the previous maize harvest. I'll use the improved variety — the seed station in the township sells Jimai varieties that yield well here and don't lodge badly in wind. I've tried traditional seed before, and the yield is just not worth it anymore. After maize harvest I'll do a rotary pass to chop the stalks and loosen the soil before planting. I always apply base fertilizer at sowing — mostly diammonium phosphate and urea — then topdress at jointing stage with urea. Three irrigations are my habit: once before winter sets in to protect roots from freezing, once at jointing, and once at heading. I watch for powdery mildew every spring — one fungicide spray around heading, and one herbicide in early spring when the weeds start. That's two pesticide runs.

**Maize follows immediately after wheat in June.** I don't plow — there's no time between wheat harvest and maize sowing if I want full-season growth before October cold. I've been no-tilling summer maize for about ten years now. I use hybrid seed, same as every farmer around here — Zhengdan or Xianyu, whichever the seed shop has. Maize gets summer rain, so I only irrigate once at emergence if the ground is dry. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then topdress urea at the big flare stage. Two pesticide runs: one herbicide early, one for corn borer in August.
